fact_en:
Why do some bars on a marimba or xylophone sound lower or higher?

Longer bars vibrate slowly for a lower pitch, while shorter bars vibrate faster for a higher pitch!
fact_bis:
Ngano nga lahi-lahi ang tunog sa mga bar sa marimba ug xylophone?

Ang mas taas nga bar nagalingkod nga hinay para sa mas ubos nga pitch, samtang ang mas mubo nagalingkod nga paspas para sa mas taas nga pitch!

findings.note: Marimba/xylophone. "Ang mas taas nga bar NAGALINGKOD nga hinay... ang mas mubo NAGALINGKOD nga paspas" — 'sits slowly / sits fast'. The entire answer to the question (long bars vibrate slowly = lower pitch) is destroyed; vibration is never named anywhere else in the card.

fact_en: Mix every paint colour together and they absorb more wavelengths of light — almost nothing reflects back, so you get a dark, muddy colour close to black!
fact_bis: Pagkat-on nimo ang tanang kolor sa pintura, magsipsip sila og daghang wavelength sa suga — gamay ra ang mobalik, maong mogawas ang madulom ug malapot nga kolor nga duol sa itim!

findings.note: "Mix every paint colour together" becomes "PAGKAT-ON nimo ang tanang kolor sa pintura" — pagkat-on = to LEARN. The card's entire fact is what happens when you MIX all paints; as written the cause is learning the colours, and neither the rest of the body nor the title ("Tanan Pintura Putik Mug-it") ever says mix/sagol. A child cannot answer "what happens when you mix all the paint colours?" from this card, and is told a false causal chain (learning colours -> they absorb wavelengths).

fact_en: In a transverse wave, particles vibrate perpendicular to the wave's travel direction! It's just like waves on a shaken rope or light waves.
fact_bis: Sa transverse wave, ang mga particle nagalingkod perpendicular sa direksyon sa pagbiyahe sa alon! Sama kini sa mga alon sa pinayog nga pisi ug mga suga.

findings.note: "particles vibrate perpendicular" becomes "ang mga particle NAGALINGKOD perpendicular" — lingkod = to SIT. The card is the definition of a transverse wave, so the verb IS the fact: as written it says the particles sit still (static) rather than oscillate, which is the opposite of wave motion. The card never uses mokurog/mag-vibrate anywhere to restore it. (Same mistranslation recurs in ffct-25507 "Dali kining nagalingkod" for vibrating vocal cords, but there the short/thin-cords -> high-pitch fact still survives, so only this one is flagged.)

fact_en:
Why can you see a flashlight beam in a dusty room?

It's the Tyndall effect! Light scatters off tiny particles in the air like dust or smoke, making the beam visible!
fact_bis:
Ngano nga makita ang flashlight beam sa maitom nga kwarto nga abogon?

Kini ang Tyndall effect! Ang suga nagawagtang sa gagmayng particles sa hangin sama sa abog o usok, makita ang beam!

findings.note: EN: "Light scatters off tiny particles in the air like dust or smoke, making the beam visible!" BIS: "Ang suga nagawagtang sa gagmayng particles sa hangin sama sa abog o usok, makita ang beam!" In Cebuano wagtang is to remove/make vanish — the corpus uses it that way on all 28 cards (sabon nagwagtang sa mikrobyo, pagwagtang sa plema). A Cebuano-only child is taught the opposite mechanism: the light DESTROYS the dust, rather than bouncing off it. Scattering is the whole content of the Tyndall card, and nothing in the Cebuano restores it (the siblings ffct-25296/25478 carry the same swap for Rayleigh scattering).

fact_en: Place your hand on your throat while speaking to feel the vibration! This confirms your voice is made by vibrating vocal cords.
fact_bis: Ibutang ang imong kamot sa tutunlan samtang nagasulti aron mabatyagan ang vibration! Nagpamatuod kini nga ang imong boses gihimo sa nagalingkod nga vocal cords.

findings.note: EN: "your voice is made by vibrating vocal cords." BIS: "ang imong boses gihimo sa nagalingkod nga vocal cords." Lingkod is to SIT — 85 corpus cards use it only that way (naglingkod, molingkod sa iyang mga itlog), while vibrate is mouyog/mokurog, which this same batch uses correctly (ffct-25582 nagakurog, ffct-25586 mauyog, ffct-25588 nag-uyog). The card's single teaching claim becomes "your voice is made by seated vocal cords"; the earlier sentence only says to feel a vibration at the throat, never that the cords are what vibrates.

fact_en:
How do glow-in-the-dark ceiling stars shine in the dark?

They absorb light when the room is bright and slowly release it in the dark! This happens because of phosphorescence in the material.
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagsilaw sa glow-in-the-dark nga mga bituin sa kisame sa kangitngit?

Nagsipsip sila og suga kung hayag ug hinay-hinay ginhawa sa kangitngit! Mahitabo kini tungod sa phosphorescence sa materyal.

findings.note: EN: "They absorb light when the room is bright and slowly release it in the dark!" BIS: "Nagsipsip sila og suga kung hayag ug hinay-hinay ginhawa sa kangitngit!" Ginhawa is breath/to breathe — all 93 corpus uses are breathing; release is mopagawas/magbuhi (34 cards). The object (the stored light) is also dropped, so the Cebuano answer never says the stars give the light back out; the child is told they "slowly breathe in the dark", and phosphorescence is left unexplained.

fact_en: A screw makes it easier to hold two things together or lift things; it turns a twisting motion into a strong forward force!
fact_bis: Ang screw nagpasayon sa paghugpong sa duha ka butang o pagpataas sa tubig; gibalhin niini ang pagtuyok ngadto sa kusog nga puwersa!

findings.note: EN: "A screw makes it easier to hold two things together or lift things; it turns a twisting motion into a strong forward force". BIS: "...paghugpong sa duha ka butang o PAGPATAAS SA TUBIG" — "lift things" became "raise WATER". Different referent, never corrected anywhere in the card; the card teaches the child that a screw's second use is raising water (an Archimedes screw), not lifting objects generally. The same clause also drops "forward" from "strong forward force" ("kusog nga puwersa" only), so the direction of the converted force is gone too.

fact_en: Meet Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit, the clever scientist who created the Fahrenheit temperature scale we use today!
fact_bis: Ilha si Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit, ang naghimo sa Fahrenheit temperature scale!

findings.note: title_bis "Fahrenheit Buhag Scale" for title_en "Fahrenheit Scale Maker". "Buhag" is not Cebuano for maker/creator (that is naghimo / magbubuhat); it looks like a corruption of "buhat" and as written carries no usable meaning, so the title alone does not say that Fahrenheit MADE the scale. The card's own body uses the correct word — "ang naghimo sa Fahrenheit temperature scale" — which is what marks the title as the outlier. Lowest-confidence of the three: the body does restore the fact, so this is a title-standalone defect, not a body falsehood.

fact_en: James Watt greatly improved the steam engine! He made it work much better and more efficiently.
fact_bis: Gipalambo pag-ayo ni James Watt ang steam engine (makina nga gipalihok sa aso)! Gihimo niya kini mas maayo ug mas episyente.

findings.note: EN: "James Watt greatly improved the steam engine". BIS glosses it as "steam engine (makina nga gipalihok sa aso)" — aso in Cebuano is SMOKE, not steam (alisngaw/singaw). The gloss is the only Cebuano explanation of what drives the engine, and nothing in the card corrects it, so a Cebuano-only child learns a steam engine is smoke-powered. The corpus's own convention contradicts it: ffct-25820 and ffct-25821 (same batch, same topic) both say "makinang de-singaw", and ffct-25763 uses "alisngaw" correctly for steam.

fact_en:
What does Gregorio Zara's videophone do?

It shows the face of the person you're talking to, just like a modern video call!
fact_bis:
Unsay gihimo sa videophone ni Gregorio Zara?

Nagpakita kini sa nawong sa imong kausap, sama ra sa video call karon!

findings.note: title_bis "Videophone Nawong Kausab" for title_en "Zara Videophone Face Call". Kausab/kausaban means CHANGE in Cebuano and is used that way throughout the corpus ("kausaban sa klima" = climate change, "makausab og kolor" = can change colour), so the title reads "Videophone Face Change" - a different thing from showing the face of the person you are talking to. The body's repair word is itself not Cebuano ("nawong sa imong kausap" is Tagalog; Cebuano is kaistorya), so neither field names the referent correctly; only the trailing "sama ra sa video call karon" rescues the fact.

fact_en: The cheetah is the absolute fastest land animal on Earth, zooming and running at about 110 km/h!
fact_bis: Ang cheetah mao ang pinakapaspas nga hayop sa tibuok yuta, makadagan og grabe ka paspas, mga 110 km/h!

findings.note: en "The cheetah is the absolute fastest LAND animal on Earth" -> bis "Ang cheetah mao ang pinakapaspas nga hayop sa tibuok yuta" = "the fastest animal in the whole world". The load-bearing qualifier "land" is gone and the Cebuano sentence is simply false (a peregrine falcon is far faster). Only the keyword-salad title ("Cheetah 110 km/h Yuta Hayop") hints at "land animal", and a sibling card in the corpus keeps it properly ("Cheetah Labing Malaksi Yuta"). A Cebuano-only child ends up believing the cheetah is the fastest animal that exists.

fact_en: Want to know how tough a rock is? The Mohs scale measures the hardness of minerals!
fact_bis: Gusto ba nimo mahibal-an kung paila ka katig-a ang bato? Ang Mohs scale nagsukod sa hardness sa mga mineral!

findings.note: title_bis "Mohs Scale Kagwang Mineral Bato" for "Mohs Measures Hardness". Kagwang is the Philippine flying lemur/colugo, an ANIMAL, not a property - the same corpus uses it that way (ffct-00185 title_bis "Kagwang"/title_en "Colugo"; ffct-01101 "Ang kagwang o Philippine flying lemur"). Cebuano for hardness is katig-a, and this card's OWN body uses it correctly ("kung paila ka katig-a ang bato", "nagsukod sa hardness sa mga mineral") - strongest evidence the title is the outlier. A child sees a rock-hardness card headed with an animal's name.
